section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Complex Plane
section_1.content: Introduce the complex plane where the x-axis is 'Real' and the y-axis is 'Imaginary'. Visualize a point (a, b) as a vector with length r and angle θ, mapping to a + bi.
section_1.example: Represent the position of a 'Drone' on a 2D grid: its distance from home (r) and its compass heading (θ).

section_2.title: The Power of Rotation
section_2.content: Explain that multiplying by i performs a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Introduce the exponential function e^x and reveal that e^(ix) acts as a 'rotation operator' on the complex plane.
section_2.example: A 'Clock Hand' that starts at 1. Multiplying by i moves it to 12 o'clock, then 9 o'clock, then 6 o'clock.

section_3.title: Deriving Euler’s Formula
section_3.content: Present Euler’s Formula: e^(ix) = cos(x) + i*sin(x). Use a visual animation showing the 'unit circle' where as x increases, the point traverses the circle's circumference.
section_3.example: A 'Firefly' flying in a perfect circle around the origin; its coordinates at any time are defined by the cosine and sine of the time elapsed.

section_4.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
section_4.content: Plug x = π into the formula. Since cos(π) = -1 and sin(π) = 0, the equation simplifies to e^(πi) = -1. Explain this as a 180-degree half-turn around the origin.
section_4.example: A 'Robot' facing East (at 1) performs a half-turn rotation (π radians). It is now facing West (at -1).

section_5.title: Summary and Elegance
section_5.content: Highlight why this is 'The Most Beautiful Equation'—it connects five fundamental mathematical constants (e, π, i, 1, 0) in one simple, elegant expression.
section_5.example: Display the equation as a 'Mathematical Rosetta Stone' that bridges the gap between arithmetic, geometry, and analysis.
